item.title: China's innovation-related investment holds steady despite broader fixed-asset decline
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's investment in innovation-driven sectors held up well in the first three quarters of 2026, even as overall fixed-asset investment continued to contract, official data showed on Monday. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.3 percent year on year in the Jan.-Sept. period, while investment in high-tech industries grew 4.9 percent, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said in a statement. Notably, several sectors posted particularly strong gains. Investment in information services surged 20.2 percent from a year earlier, and aerospace equipment manufacturing investment climbed 12.5 percent, while investment in electronic and communications equipment manufacturing rose 7.6 percent. The resilience of these sectors stands in contrast to the broader investment picture. Total fixed-asset investment fell 7.2 percent year on year to 33.41 trillion yuan (4.97 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first three quarters of 2026, dragged down in part by a slump in real estate investment. Excluding real estate development investment, total fixed-asset investment declined 4.2 percent. In breakdown, infrastructure investment fell 4.2 percent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, manufacturing investment dropped 2.1 percent, and real estate development investment declined 20.6 percent in this period. Private sector investment, meanwhile, contracted by 10.4 percent. While overall growth has slowed, investment is playing an increasingly important role in optimizing supply and driving innovation, Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS, told a press conference on Monday. Analysts said the current pullback in overall investment reflects a transition from a traditional investment model to a new one. "Investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, and from scale expansion to efficiency improvement," said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics. China's effective investment space remains vast over the medium and long term, Liu said, noting that artificial intelligence (AI) and new infrastructure will serve as key engines for the next round of effective investment. The expansion of AI applications is spurring sustained investment across industrial chains. NBS data revealed that in the first three quarters of 2026, investment in electronic circuit manufacturing surged 58.7 percent year on year, and integrated circuit manufacturing investment rose 14.2 percent. Meanwhile, companies are accelerating their shift toward intelligent operations, driving a 9.7 percent increase in investment in equipment and tools purchases. In terms of new infrastructure, China's "six networks" initiative, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks, represents a major investment opportunity. It is estimated that investment in these six networks and related areas will exceed 7 trillion yuan in 2026. Investment will increasingly serve the development of new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system, with the ultimate results felt in expanded employment, rising incomes and improved living standards, Liu said. ■

item.title: China's integrated computing network spurs new industrial opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's national integrated computing power network is unleashing new industrial opportunities, supported by an increasingly complete industrial chain spanning upstream hardware, midstream platforms, and a widening range of downstream applications. Chinese central authorities have recently issued a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces to bolster high-quality development. The guidelines outlined multiple key sectors for advancing the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy, including building a national integrated computing power network and a nationwide blockchain network, among other initiatives. Coordinated computing power development in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region is a good example of China's comprehensive advancement in building a national network. By now, 36 data centers have been established in Langfang City, north China's Hebei Province, roughly a one-hour drive from Beijing. These data centers are serving China's tech giants like Huawei and JD.com, as well as other companies. Computing resources here also meet the real-time computing demands of Beijing's sci-tech innovation industries, internet sector, and other sectors. Building on the coordinated layout and construction of the national integrated computing power network, regions across the country are stepping up efforts to build and optimize computing hubs, data centers, and computing network nodes, while accelerating computing-electricity coordination and computing-network integration. Other regions are also capitalizing on their strengths to gain a foothold in niche markets and pursue differentiated development. The Lichuan AI Computing Center is nestled in the Wuling Mountains of Lichuan City, central China's Hubei Province. Its services cover culture and tourism, government affairs, and aerospace information. This city is not endowed with abundant scientific or educational resources, but its mountainous location, cool climate and rich hydropower resources make it an ideal place for a computing center with relatively low electricity costs. In Liangwu Township of Lichuan, a satellite ground receiving station has been built by GEOVIS Raywin Technology Co., Ltd. It allows instant access to computing power from the adjacent AI computing center when receiving and processing satellite data. "The station's proximity to the computing center enhances the operational efficiency, convenience, and cost-effectiveness," said Gao Kui, the company's general manager of operations. By the end of June this year, China's intelligent computing capacity had risen 177 percent year on year to reach 2,185 EFLOPS. EFLOPS refers to a unit measuring computing performance, with each unit representing 1 quintillion floating-point operations per second. By then, more than 70 computing transmission channels connecting computing hubs and key regions had been built, according to data from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. China is accelerating the construction of an integrated national computing power platform, aiming to enhance the quality and efficiency of computing resources and strengthen the country's capabilities in core technologies such as AI chips. The China computing power platform has now achieved integrated nationwide computing power monitoring and coordination. It has listed over 2,000 computing products and connected to more than 300 large models, providing AI developers with on-demand access to computing power. "A national integrated computing power network is not a simple pile-up of computing resources, but is connecting computing power, electricity, data, models, and scenarios into an infrastructure network for the intelligent economy," said Li Mingyan, an analyst at the industrial research institute of consulting firm CIO Manage. This platform can meet the diverse needs of application scenarios such as large AI model training, autonomous driving, smart finance, and low-altitude economy. Also, through the "East Data, West Computing" project and cross-regional computing power scheduling, it better matches the green electricity resources in the country's western regions with the computing power demand in the eastern regions, lowering the cost of computing use and promoting the consumption of green energy, according to Li. As a national strategy, China's "East Data, West Computing" project operates similarly to a power grid, shifting the heavy data processing demands of the country's economically bustling eastern coast to resource-rich western regions. It utilizes the west's abundant green energy such as wind and hydropower, making it a major milestone in green technology and carbon reduction. Industry experts said that industrial opportunities will gradually emerge along the upstream, midstream and downstream of the national computing network. For example, the large-scale construction of computing clusters will drive demand for AI chips, high-speed optical modules, and green energy facilities. In addition, services ranging from computing power scheduling and model inference optimization to token-based metering and billing are expected to spur the growth of new platform companies. "At the application level, the network will sustain intelligent upgrading across industries and help innovate businesses in areas of the token economy, cloud computers, and cloud phones," said Li Wei, a researcher at the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. The network also helps lower the barriers to digitalization and AI adoption for small and medium-sized enterprises, and improve quality and performance of traditional industries, she added. ■

item.title: China's Q3 economy picks up pace, reinforcing role as global growth engine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
* China's GDP grew 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support. * New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. * More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains. BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's economy picked up pace in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support, staying on track to meet its annual growth target and remaining a leading engine of global growth. China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5 percent year on year in Q3, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed Monday. The world's second-largest economy generated about 107.11 trillion yuan (about 15.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in output during the January-September period, expanding 4.6 percent year on year, according to the NBS. "The national economy forged ahead against pressure and continued to shift toward innovation-driven, high-quality development, with growing positive changes in major indicators," the NBS said in a statement. China has consistently contributed around 30 percent of global economic growth, with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva saying in January that this contribution is expected to stay at roughly the same level in the coming years. GROWING RESILIENCE Noting that the GDP growth of 4.6 percent in the first three quarters is in line with the country's annual growth target, NBS deputy head Mao Shengyong told a media conference that the economy added 5.7 trillion yuan in output during the period, the largest increase for the same period in the past five years. In the third quarter, GDP growth picked up 0.2 percentage points from the second quarter, while some international institutions expected major economies to grow more slowly in July-September compared to the April-June period, Mao said. There was also a notable rise in momentum on a monthly basis. In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points faster than in August, while the services production index gained 4.8 percent, up 0.7 percentage points from the previous month. Retail sales of consumer goods grew 1.1 percent in September, 0.7 percentage points faster than in August, and the surveyed urban unemployment rate edged down 0.1 percentage points from August to 5.2 percent. "Growth momentum showed signs of marginal improvement in September," said Wen Bin, chief economist with China Minsheng Bank, citing faster industrial and services output, a rebound in consumption and an initial stabilization of investment. China will step up efforts to expand domestic demand, improve supply, and make macro policies more effective to sustain the positive momentum of innovation-led and high-quality development, Mao said. To this end, China has recently rolled out a batch of new policies, including financial and fiscal support. "With existing policies being implemented faster and incremental policies gradually taking effect, the economy is expected to continue improving in the fourth quarter," Wen said. NEW DRIVERS AT WORK New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. Value-added industrial output rose 5.3 percent year on year, with equipment manufacturing up 10.2 percent and high-tech manufacturing up 14.3 percent. Output of industrial robots, lithium-ion batteries and 3D printing equipment jumped 29.1 percent, 39.5 percent and 62.5 percent, respectively. Monday's data also showed that the services sector expanded 5.2 percent year on year in the first three quarters, with information transmission, software and IT services up 10.4 percent, and leasing and business services up 12.3 percent. The shift is visible in the economic structure. Manufacturing accounted for 25.7 percent of GDP in the first three quarters, up 0.6 percentage points from a year earlier, while the share of high-tech manufacturing in the value-added output of major industrial enterprises rose 1.6 percentage points. Investment in intellectual property products climbed 9.3 percent. Traditional industries are also moving up the value chain. In Jingdezhen, a ceramics hub in east China's Jiangxi Province, local producers have embraced 3D printing in pottery making, propelling the sector's output to over 100 billion yuan. Meanwhile, some coal mining companies have implemented smart monitoring systems for underground operations, increasing efficiency by 30 percent. Green development is creating openings as well. The penetration rate of new energy vehicles in China has stayed above 60 percent for six consecutive months, while the country's energy consumption per unit of GDP fell 3.1 percent in the first three quarters. "The foundations of the economy remain solid, while new quality productive forces, modern services and high-tech foreign trade are steadily taking root," said Zhu Qigui, associate director of the China Academy of Financial Research. "As long as China continues to rely on innovation, reform and its vast market, the trend of moving toward new and better development will not change," the scholar said. SHARED OPPORTUNITIES A major trading partner of as many as 169 countries and regions, China saw its goods trade rise 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the first three quarters. In September alone, trade grew 27.5 percent. In the first nine months, exports of mechanical and electrical products climbed 23.7 percent and accounted for 64.3 percent of total exports, while intermediate goods made up more than half of all exports, reinforcing China's role as a stabilizing anchor for global industrial and supply chains. In east China's Anhui Province, robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd. has continued to see growth in overseas orders this year, with a batch of its spraying robots set to be exported to Italy. The company's overseas revenue increased by more than 50 percent year on year in the first half of 2026. Meanwhile, the company's client, German automobile giant Volkswagen, is shifting its strategy from "in China, for China" to "in China, beyond China," with cars produced in China already exported to the Middle East and Central Asia. Foreign-invested enterprises in China remained active players in the January-September period, with their imports and exports rising 19 percent to 11.69 trillion yuan, a record high for the same period. Their trade in intermediate goods grew 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan, and their high-tech product exports jumped 42.1 percent. More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains, Mao said. ■ (Video editors: Hong Liang and Zhu Cong)

item.title: China condemns Japan's negative moves concerning Yasukuni Shrine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China firmly opposes and strongly condemns Japan's negative moves concerning the Yasukuni Shrine, and has lodged stern representations and strong protests with the Japanese side, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said Monday. Spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a daily media briefing in Beijing after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a ritual offering and monetary donation to the Yasukuni Shrine on Oct. 17 and 19, while multiple Japanese government officials, senior officials of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and parliamentarians paid visits to the site recently. Mao stressed that the Yasukuni Shrine is a spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarists responsible for the war of aggression, and the place honors 14 convicted Class-A war criminals with grave responsibilities for the war crimes committed during that war of aggression. "The Japanese leaders and politicians are fully aware of these facts, yet they still pay tribute to the Yasukuni Shrine in a high-sounding manner. Such acts lay bare their deep-rooted erroneous perceptions on historical issues, as well as their sinister attempt to exonerate war criminals, reverse the verdict on aggression and pave the way for remilitarization," Mao said. Noting this year marks 80 years of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, the spokesperson once again solemnly urged Japan to face up to history, reflect on its crimes, stop retrogressive acts on historical issues, and win trust from its Asian neighbors and the international community with concrete actions. ■

item.title: China rolls out measures to spur consumption through tech innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on accelerating technology-driven commerce, in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Pan Xu) BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China has released new guidelines to promote the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and other advanced technologies in commerce, as part of efforts to expand consumer demand, upgrade traditional businesses and improve the efficiency of goods distribution. These guidelines, jointly issued by nine government departments, including the Ministry of Commerce, outline 18 measures covering goods consumption, services consumption, commercial distribution, innovative business applications and policy support. "The move aims to meet the immediate need to boost consumption and invigorate the consumer market, while using technology-driven innovation to upgrade traditional commerce and foster emerging business models," Yuan Xiaoming, assistant minister of commerce, told a press conference on Monday. To upgrade consumer goods, the guidelines call for integrating AI into product development, design, manufacturing and marketing, expanding the supply of smart devices and robots, and encouraging flexible manufacturing and AI-powered customization. New technologies, including AI, the Internet of Things and blockchain, can help drive consumption upgrades, Yuan said. Data from the ministry showed that sales of smart glasses on major platforms rose 110 percent year on year in January-September 2026. The measures also encourage the use of AI in healthcare and smart elderly care services, as well as the digital transformation of catering businesses, to expand services consumption. China's retail sales of consumer goods rose 1.1 percent year on year to 37 trillion yuan (about 5.5 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first three quarters of 2026, while retail sales of services increased 5 percent, outpacing the 1-percent growth in retail sales of goods, official data released on Monday showed. To create more personalized consumer experiences, the guidelines support emerging intelligent services such as companion robots. They also promote the use of ultra-high-definition audiovisual technology and digital twins in shopping districts, tourism, education and training. They also call for pilot applications of AI in culture and tourism, as immersive experiences and digital performances gain traction in China's cultural and tourism market. Data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed that revenue from emerging cultural sectors grew 9.6 percent year on year in the first half of 2026, 5 percentage points faster than the overall cultural industry. In commercial distribution, the measures promote smart warehouses, intelligent logistics equipment and unmanned delivery, alongside digital upgrades in wholesale and retail businesses. The guidelines also call for developing commercial AI agents for shopping assistance, business operations and logistics, expanding applications of embodied intelligence, and creating virtual shopping experiences. They additionally outline support for technology standards, digital infrastructure and financing. The new measures build on China's broader push to accelerate the commercial application of AI and other advanced technologies. China's AI industry has expanded rapidly, with AI-powered smartphones, intelligent connected vehicles and humanoid robots among the products seeing broader application. The country's AI core industry was estimated to have exceeded 1.2 trillion yuan in 2025. In late 2025, China launched a special initiative to integrate AI into manufacturing. AI adoption among large industrial firms has since exceeded 30 percent, said Wei Wei, an official from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. China will further develop the AI industry and expand its application in manufacturing, focusing on key AI technologies and the development of intelligent devices such as brain-computer interfaces and embodied AI systems, Wei added. ■

item.title: Resilient Chinese economy brings much-needed certainty to the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Viewed as an ocean rather than a pond, China's economy may not be immune to headwinds, but it stands firm enough to absorb powerful waves and weather turbulent times. In a world starved of certainty, it remains a stabilizing force in the global economy. Facts on the ground speak for themselves. China's economy expanded by 4.6 percent in the first three quarters of 2026, landing squarely within the full-year target range and remaining among the fastest of major economies. Yet to read the economy solely through the lens of headline speed is to miss the more important story. China is in a critical period of accelerating the transition from old growth drivers to new ones. The quality of growth and the direction of structural change matter more. New quality productive forces are gathering momentum, with new growth drivers including high-end manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy and modern services contributing more than 40 percent of expansion. In particular, industrial robots, 3D-printing equipment and lithium-ion batteries all registered strong double-digit growth, helping steer the economy toward more innovation-led, quality-driven development. The foundation of China's economic resilience also lies in consumption, which accounted for nearly half of the GDP growth in the first three quarters. Services retail sales, upgraded goods consumption, new formats, as well as lower-tier markets and inbound tourism, are all picking up steam. With policymakers leaning harder into consumption support, household spending appetite is showing steady signs of recovery, setting the stage to unlock the vast potential of the country's super-large market. Foreign trade remains one of the brightest spots, with growth reaching its highest level for the same period in five years. From new energy vehicles to photovoltaic products, robotics and innovative pharmaceuticals, Chinese exports are increasingly defined by frontier technology, original innovation capability and complete industrial and supply chains. Furthermore, China has ample and effective policy tools to shape its economic growth trajectory. Five-year plans, deepened reforms and wider opening up, along with targeted fiscal and monetary measures and considerable room for counter-cyclical adjustment, all provide predictability and stability for the market. A clear-eyed understanding of the Chinese economy also requires acknowledging the real headwinds: a complex and volatile external environment, insufficient domestic demand, and a structural transition that isn't finished. As the latest figures have demonstrated, the Chinese economy is resilient. This is contrary to the narratives hyped up by certain pessimists and doomsters in the West. Backed by a domestic market of 1.4 billion people, a solid manufacturing base, well-developed infrastructure, a strong talent pool, and complete industrial and supply chains, the underlying fundamentals and long-term positive trend remain unchanged. Amid the sluggish global recovery and rising geopolitical risks, China's development continues to offer the world growth momentum and market opportunities. It is both a sustained driver of inclusive and shared growth and a reliable buffer against global economic volatility stemming from factors such as regional conflicts and the rise of unilateralism and protectionism. For many years, China has contributed around 30 percent of global economic growth, remaining a major engine of the world economy. As the world's largest manufacturer, China continues to provide high-quality, affordable, and reliable product supply globally. No longer just the world's factory, China is becoming a market and a mega-buyer for the world as imports have surged over 20 percent, reflecting a more balanced and open trade structure. China's commitment to opening up remains unwavering despite rising protectionism globally. This is evidenced by the establishment of more new foreign-invested enterprises, and also highlighted by Apple's executive chairman Tim Cook, who recently noted that the company remains optimistic about China's development prospects and will further expand its business in the country. China's edge may lie less in its speed, but more in the quality and sustainability of its advance, and in its capacity to hit its full-year targets. "China Opportunity 2.0," boosted by the dividends of innovation and high-standard opening up, will surely create more win-win cooperation outcomes for the world. ■

item.title: Chinese premier says ready to expand cooperation with Tajikistan in emerging industries
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Tajik President Emomali Rahmon in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, Oct. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) DUSHANBE, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said Monday that China is willing to expand cooperation with Tajikistan in emerging industries such as the digital economy and artificial intelligence. In his meeting with Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, Li said China stands ready to expand bilateral trade with Tajikistan, strengthen cooperation in infrastructure, green minerals, connectivity and other fields, so as to jointly build new drivers of economic growth. He called for deepening cooperation with Tajikistan in law enforcement and security, saying both sides should strengthen intelligence exchanges and information sharing, jointly combat the three forces of terrorism, separatism and extremism, and safeguard lasting peace and stability in the region. The Chinese premier expressed hope that the Tajik side will continue to take strong measures to ensure the safety and security of Chinese personnel and enterprises in Tajikistan. Li arrived here on Sunday for an official visit to Tajikistan and the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO). In talks with the Tajik president, he said China will fully support Tajikistan in successfully hosting the SCO meeting, and stands ready to work with all parties to promote higher-quality development of the SCO. China is also willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Tajikistan within the United Nations, the China-Central Asia mechanism and other multilateral frameworks, actively implement the four global initiatives proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity, he said. The premier noted that China and Tajikistan are currently advancing efforts to build a community with a shared future between the two countries, and in May this year, President Xi met with President Rahmon, providing further guidance for the development of bilateral relations. China cherishes its profound friendship with Tajikistan and will always view China-Tajikistan relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, Li said. China stands ready to consolidate and deepen political mutual trust with Tajikistan, firmly support each other's core interests, continuously enhance the quality and effectiveness of cooperation, and continue to work hand in hand on the path toward modernization, he added. Noting that Tajikistan always attaches great importance to and highly values its partnership with China, Rahmon said that in May this year, he successfully held talks with President Xi during his visit to China and reached a series of important consensus, charting the course for the development of Tajikistan-China relations. Tajikistan firmly adheres to the one-China principle and firmly supports China in safeguarding its core interests, the president noted. Rahmon said that Tajikistan is willing to further deepen cooperation with China in areas such as economy and trade, industry, agriculture, energy and minerals, connectivity and artificial intelligence, and promote people-to-people and cultural exchanges. Tajikistan firmly supports the four major global initiatives proposed by President Xi, said Rahmon, noting that Tajikistan stands ready to enhance coordination with China within multilateral frameworks including the United Nations, the SCO and the China-Central Asia Mechanism, advance the Tajikistan-China comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership in the new era to new heights, and work together to build a community with a shared future for the two countries. ■ Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Tajik President Emomali Rahmon in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, Oct. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Ding Lin)

item.title: Xi-proposed principles provide practical guidance for settling Africa's hotspot issues: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Four principles proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping on the constructive participation of relevant parties in the resolution of African hotspot issues provide practical guidance for addressing issues including the current situation in the Horn of Africa, a foreign ministry spokesperson said on Monday. Xi put forward the principles during his meeting with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé in Beijing last week. When asked whether this was related to the current situation in northern Ethiopia, Mao Ning, the spokesperson, told a regular press briefing that the principles provide practical guidance for addressing issues including the current situation in the Horn of Africa. First, upholding Africa's leadership, Mao said, citing the principles. "African people are the true masters of the continent and should therefore play a central role in regional affairs." Second, safeguarding equity and justice. Parties should observe the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of countries concerned, she said. Third, ceasing hostilities and building peace. "War and unilateral sanctions are never real solutions to disputes between states. Countries should respect each other, engage in extensive consultation, seek common ground despite differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation," Mao said. "Fourth, addressing both symptoms and root causes. Addressing immediate security concerns should go hand in hand with long-term development planning," the spokesperson said. ■
